clue.text: Start factory, mostly having no dividing walls

parts.note: to open something is to start it

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: Someone launching a factory whose workspace has no internal walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter, T, from PLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan office or home is laid out without internal partition walls.

clue.text: Team following forward, working towards the same goal

indicators.note: following means the team comes after the forward

parts.note: on means forward, as in 'move on'
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A footballer playing behind the striker, both aiming at one goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' and 'goal' suggest football, where onside means legally positioned; here it means on the same side.
explanation.definitionFit: To be onside is to be in agreement and supporting a shared aim.

clue.text: Reminiscent of Marlowe's last case

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the word Marlowe's, before the possessive

parts.note: the vocative is a grammatical case, used in addressing someone

explanation.surface: Recalling the final investigation of detective Philip Marlowe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a detective's case; it is a grammatical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative brings memories or images to mind, being suggestive of them.

clue.text: Defeated chief US rate badly is forced to retire

parts.note: put out means dismissed or defeated, as a batsman is
top means chief

indicators.note: badly says these letters are put wrong, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A defeated American bank boss whose rate went badly is pushed into retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Put out to pasture is an idiom from retiring old farm animals, applied to people made to stop work.

clue.text: American ringing pal in Nato, perhaps

indicators.note: ringing means encircling the next piece

parts.note: a crony is a pal

explanation.surface: A US caller telephoning a friend at the military alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like telephoning but means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is a word formed from initials, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.

clue.text: Viewing instruments to manage on board steamship

indicators.note: being on board a ship means being inside it, so these letters sit within the vessel's abbreviation

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Telescopes and the like brought aboard a steamer to be operated.
explanation.definitionFit: Scopes is a general word for optical instruments such as telescopes and microscopes.

clue.text: Game of chess where pin is disastrous

indicators.note: a disastrous position is a wrecked one, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A chess game where pinning a piece proves calamitous.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a party game where a message is whispered along a line and garbled.

clue.text: Daughter impressed by Ring Cycle?

indicators.note: impressed means pressed into, so the daughter's letter goes inside

parts.note: a peal is a ring of bells

explanation.surface: A daughter moved by Wagner's Ring Cycle operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring Cycle' suggests Wagner; split it, and 'Cycle' as a verb is the definition, flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To cycle is to ride a bicycle, which is done by working the foot levers.

clue.text: Drink in hotel entertained by upwardly mobile salesmen?

indicators.note: entertained by means held as a guest within the next piece
upwardly in a down clue means the word reads from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
the Ritz is a famous London hotel

explanation.surface: A drink at a hotel bar hosted by ambitious sales staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwardly mobile' looks like ambitious but, in a down clue, reads the salesmen bottom to top as SPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is a drink of white wine mixed with soda water.

clue.text: This could be the beginning, or be my undoing

indicators.note: undoing means taking these letters apart and putting them back differently

explanation.surface: Someone musing that an event could start something or ruin them.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryo is the earliest stage of an organism's development, its starting point.

clue.text: Third of cast left play

indicators.note: third of picks out the third letter of the following word

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A drama note: one of three cast members has walked out of the play.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport is to play or frolic, an old-fashioned sense of the verb.

clue.text: Jogger grabbing a rest

indicators.note: grabbing means holding the next piece inside the first

parts.note: something that jogs the memory is a reminder

explanation.surface: A runner seizing a moment's breather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' looks like a runner but means a memory-jogger.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest of something is what is left over, its remainder.

clue.text: Nervously order a nun to leave in a hurry

indicators.note: nervously suggests jittery, disordered movement, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A jittery instruction telling a nun to get out quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a runner is a British informal idiom for fleeing, often without paying.

clue.text: Story about one capsizing in Israeli port

indicators.note: capsizing in a down-reading sense turns the whole construction backwards
about means going round the next piece

parts.note: a tale is a story
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tale of a boat overturning near an Israeli harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside TALE to make TALIE, and 'capsizing' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eilat is Israel's port at the northern tip of the Red Sea.

clue.text: Injured party in casualty

definitions.meaning: the person wronged or harmed in a dispute or crime
someone killed or hurt in an accident or war

explanation.surface: A wounded person being treated in the hospital emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casualty' is also the British name for a hospital emergency department, which the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe a person who has suffered harm or loss.

clue.text: Extra expected is late arriving

parts.note: over means extra, as in left over
due means expected, as a train is due

explanation.surface: An additional delivery that was anticipated hasn't turned up on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has not arrived by the time it was expected.

clue.text: Pistol produced by the German impostor

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a ringer is an impostor, especially one entered in a race under a false identity

explanation.surface: A gun produced by a German fraudster.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small, short-barrelled pocket handgun.

clue.text: A female, smooth-spoken and well-to-do

parts.note: fluent speech is smooth and effortless

explanation.surface: A wealthy, articulate woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent and well-to-do both mean wealthy.

clue.text: Appropriate gathering bound for bughouse

indicators.note: gathering means taking the next piece in, enclosing it

parts.note: fit means appropriate or suitable
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: A suitable assembly heading off to an insect house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' means enclosing, not a meeting. 'Appropriate' looks like a verb meaning take, but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Bughouse and fleapit are both slang for a shabby, run-down cinema.

clue.text: Type of sauce served up in Minnesota motel

indicators.note: served up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sauce on the menu at a roadside lodge in Minnesota.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue, 'served up' reads the letters from the bottom up; 'in' signals that they sit inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato is a common variety of sauce, such as ketchup.

clue.text: Circle globe

definitions.meaning: a social circle or field of activity
a round solid body, like a ball

explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle' here is a social set, a sphere of influence or society.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a field of social activity and a ball-shaped body share this word.

clue.text: Initially such bravery shown, after dropping a whip

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of such
dropping means the letter A falls out of the word

parts.note: courage is bravery

explanation.surface: Courage displayed once someone let go of a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip used for punishment.

clue.text: Enthusiastic male team heading off

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: a party is a group or team of people

explanation.surface: An eager man as his team sets out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty describes a vigorous, cheerfully enthusiastic manner.

clue.text: A great many surrounding uranium plant

indicators.note: surrounding means placed round the next piece

parts.note: lots means a great many
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Plenty of material encasing radioactive uranium at a power plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a nuclear plant, but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is an aquatic flowering plant, sacred in several Asian religions.

clue.text: Implied historian not with us

indicators.note: not with means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: Tacitus was a Roman historian

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a historian is not on our side.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being stated, so implied.

clue.text: Smuggled spirits? Nonsense

definitions.meaning: illicitly distilled or smuggled liquor, especially whisky

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both bootleg liquor and foolish, fanciful talk.

clue.text: Meet knight in English bar

indicators.note: in places the knight's letter inside the next pair of pieces

parts.note: a counter is a bar where drinks are served
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An invitation to meet a knight in an English pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone is to meet them, often by chance.

clue.text: Keen listener describing good ending to programme

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing round, so the listener's letters encircle the rest

parts.note: an ear is a listener

indicators.note: ending to picks the final letter of the word programme

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic audience member describing a good finale to a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means tracing round, as one describes a circle: EAR goes round G and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and eager are synonyms for enthusiastic.

clue.text: Suppressed laugh from wife leaving website

indicators.note: leaving means the wife's letter departs from the website's name

parts.note: Twitter is a social media website

explanation.surface: A stifled giggle when a spouse quits social media.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a short, nervous or suppressed giggle.

clue.text: Spindrift evoked by page in a Sayers novel

indicators.note: in puts the page's letter inside the next words
novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wind-blown spray conjured up on a page of a Dorothy L. Sayers book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun for the book but is the anagram signal, rearranging ASAYERS with P.
explanation.definitionFit: Spindrift is the fine spray blown off wave crests by the wind.
